newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH PKO BP TO UP CREDIT RATES, DEPOSITS FLAT.
newsitem.headline: POLISH PKO BP TO UP CREDIT RATES, DEPOSITS FLAT.

text.p: Polish state-owned savings bank PKO BP will on September 1 increase its credit rates between 0.5 and 2.0 percent but it plans to leave deposit rates unchanged, its spokesman said on Tuesday.

"Credits for firms will rise by 0.8 and 1.5 percent, consumer credits by 0.5 and 2.0 percent, while residential and preferential credits for flood victims will be unchanged," Janusz Ostaszewski told Reuters.
He said PKO's 3-month turnover credit will rise to between 22.8-27.5 percent from the previous 22.0-26.5 percent. PKO's 12-month credit increased to 22.8-28.5 from 22.0-27.5 percent.
Rates for three-month deposits remained unchanged at 16-17 percent and at 18.5-19.5 percent for 12-month depos, he said.
PKO BP's move follows last week's increase of official rates by the central bank. The central bank increased its lombard rate by two points to 27 percent and discount by 2.5 percent to 24.5 percent.
